title: Org-scoped token refresh race causing transient authZ mismatches across Dedicated/Private customers
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Multiple customers (hosted and dedicated) reported intermittent 401/403 errors after API key rotations and during high-concurrency refreshes. Behavior: short window where new access tokens are issued but carry incorrect org-scoping (user's org id is unset or replaced), causing authorization failures or cross-org access checks to reject valid requests. Impacted paths: /v1/auth/refresh, API key rotation worker, and auth proxy cache layer on Dedicated nodes.
reproduction_steps: 1) Create two orgs in a single Dedicated cluster with rapid API key rotation enabled for one org.
2) Simulate concurrent clients (50+) sharing the same user_id but different org-scoped API keys attempting token refresh at same time.
3) Observe that some refresh responses return access tokens with missing org claim or wrong org claim leading to 403 on subsequent resource calls.
4) Reproduce more reliably by enabling auth-proxy memcache and forcing the auth service to reuse cached refresh metadata across requests (race window).
root_cause: The refresh flow used a cache key derived from user_id instead of refresh_token_id/jti. When concurrent refresh requests interleave, cached refresh-metadata (org_id, tenant_scopes) could be returned for the wrong token request. Additionally, Dedicated auth-proxy instances applied a stale JWKS key cache with delayed rotation, allowing revoked tokens to be accepted for a short window. The combination produced transient authZ mismatches and failures, especially under high concurrency and during key rotations.
mitigation: 1) Temporary customer-facing mitigation: request affected customers rotate API keys and restart auth-proxy pods on Dedicated clusters to clear local caches. For Hosted customers we blacklisted the observed compromised refresh_token_ids server-side to prevent reuse (manual block list). 2) Added emergency deploy to reduce JWKS TTL from 10m -> 30s for Dedicated control plane while we patch caching logic.
proposed_fix:
- Change refresh cache key to include refresh_token_id (jti) + client_id, not user_id.
- Persist token binding: include token jti in access tokens so we can validate binding on resource requests.
- Add atomic refresh-holder semaphore to prevent concurrent reissuance for same jti.
- Introduce server-side revocation check during refresh that references latest revocation index.
- Ensure JWKS rotation is event-driven for Dedicated and that cached keys are validated with last-rotation timestamps.
rollout_plan: Canary deploy on hosted control plane (5% traffic) with feature-flag: refresh-cache-key-v2 enabled.
Smoke tests: high-concurrency token refresh harness and API key rotation scenario in staging Dedicated replica.
Gradual rollout to Dedicated via release channel: auth-proxy v2 with TTL reduction + cache-key fix, then control-plane patch; monitor for auth error rate and token issuance anomalies.
Private (on-prem) customers: provide patch bundle and clear upgrade playbook; require customer opt-in for JWKS TTL change.
qa_acceptance_criteria: No observed 401/403 spikes in canary for refresh and subsequent resource calls under 100-concurrency refresh test.
Regression tests added covering concurrent refresh for same user across different org-scoped api-keys and asserting correct org claim in access token.
Unit tests verifying cache key construction and revocation index checks.
Load-tested Dedicated staging cluster shows failure rate <= baseline and no cross-org claim leakage.
Security review completed for token-binding changes.
postmortem_notes: Timeline: First customer report on 2025-02-08 03:12 UTC. Initial mitigation (blacklist + restart) applied 2025-02-09. Root cause identified 2025-02-10. Patch authored 2025-02-12. Canary started 2025-02-16.
Contributing factors: cache key choice (user_id), JWKS TTL too long for Dedicated, and lack of atomic refresh guard. Operations burdened by per-cluster cache divergence.

Action items: (a) ship fix in this ticket, (b) add RBAC test matrices for auth edge-cases, (c) add telemetry for per-jti refresh counts, (d) update runbooks for token rotation events, (e) schedule a postmortem review with affected customers week of 2025-02-24.
